**Gaps:**

**Recommendation:** Before applying, build foundational cloud cost management knowledge through a FinOps Foundation certification or Google Cloud FinOps coursework, then reapply when a cloud-adjacent FP&A role appears.

Hiring Manager
GitLab

Dear Hiring Manager,

When cloud and AI infrastructure costs grow quickly, finance teams need forecast models that move with the business, not behind it. At Calder Industrial Components, I faced a version of that problem: a forecast model that couldn't keep pace with operational reality. I rebuilt it around order backlog data, lifting accuracy from 88% to 96%, and that discipline of finding the right driver and building the model around it is exactly what GitLab's FP&A team needs for cloud hosting spend.

Over five years in FP&A roles, I've owned monthly forecasting, variance analysis, and month-end close reporting across business units with combined revenue of around $85 million. I've built Power BI dashboards on SAP data to turn detailed operational data into clear narratives for non-finance stakeholders, which maps directly to translating complex billing and usage data into decision-support materials for GitLab's engineering and finance leaders. I also shortened month-end close reporting from nine working days to six by automating journal checks in Excel VBA, a practical example of the kind of workflow improvement GitLab expects analysts to drive through automation. Cloud billing data is new territory for me, but working with granular, driver-based cost data and explaining results to cross-functional partners is not.

I'd welcome the chance to discuss how my forecasting and reporting background fits GitLab's FP&A team. I'm available at your convenience.

Best regards,
Tomas Brandt
